analysis: Market regime is a weak uptrend (SPY +0.2% vs SMA50, shallow slope). Portfolio is performing well overall: ADSK +10.8%, UHS +10.6%, ULTA +9.7%, FOXA +6.7% — four of five positions are healthy and thesis-intact. The weak link is AMP (-4.54%), which is notable for two reasons: (1) it did not appear in this cycle's 30 screened candidates, meaning it likely failed the quality+trend filter (possible confirmed downtrend or softening fundamentals), and (2) the loss combined with absence from the screened universe constitutes a soft thesis-break. We are at the 5-position maximum, so no new buy is possible without first exiting a position. AMP is the natural candidate given the evidence. The freed capital plus existing $20K headroom enables a full-sized entry into TE Connectivity (TEL), which is the strongest candidate in this scan: quality business (ROE 24.6%, op margin 21.1%, PEG 1.26, fwd P/E 14.4), confirmed uptrend with SMA50 slope positive, mid-range at 48% of 52w range (not extended), and analyst EPS revisions up +5.5% over 60 days with earnings 77 days away. The transition from AMP to TEL improves both the technical trend backdrop and fundamental quality of the book. Remaining positions (ADSK, FOXA, UHS, ULTA) all hold thesis; no action needed there. Cash after the swap settles near ~$11K (~11%), which is appropriate. No other candidate offers a comparably clean asymmetric setup at this stage — IBMs D/E of 185 is concerning, NXPI is +14% above SMA50 (extended), AXP has a negative SMA50 slope, and TSLA at P/E 428 fails the quality-at-fair-price test categorically.

trades.rationale: Fundamental: TE Connectivity is a high-quality industrial/technology connector and sensor business with durable competitive advantages in auto, aerospace, and industrial automation. Fwd P/E of 14.4 and PEG of 1.26 represent fair-to-cheap pricing for a business generating 24.6% ROE, 21.1% operating margins, and 11.9% revenue growth. D/E of 41 is conservative. FCF of $2.4B on a $63B market cap (3.8% yield) is solid. Analyst EPS revisions are +5.5% over the last 60 days — positive momentum in expectations. Next earnings 77 days out removes near-term binary event risk. Technical: Confirmed uptrend, SMA50 slope positive at +1.2%, currently only 3.5% above SMA50 (not overextended), and at 48% of 52-week range (mid-range, Stage 2 continuation with room to run to prior highs at $246 and beyond). Stop at 1.75x ATR ($13.83) places the floor at $205.64, a natural support zone. Position sizing: 110 shares × $219.47 = $24,142 (23.8% of equity, within 25% cap); worst-case loss = 110 × $13.83 = $1,521 = 1.5% of equity, within 1-2% heat budget.
trades.exit_plan: Exit if: (1) price closes below $205.64 stop (stop-hit, no discretion); (2) SMA50 slope turns negative for two consecutive weeks suggesting trend degradation; (3) earnings in January 2027 show revenue growth decelerating sharply below 8% or margin compression; (4) price reaches $260 target — reassess at that point for LTCG conversion if thesis remains intact and 1-year mark is approaching. Time stop: if no meaningful progress toward $240 within 90 days, re-evaluate whether capital is better deployed elsewhere.
